title: China’s Buyback Push Struggles to Put a Floor Under Stocks
summary: Chinese companies are tapping only a fraction of loans provided by Beijing for stock buybacks, an indication that the latest effort to support markets is faltering.

title: Asian Stocks Track US Losses Before Nvidia Results: Markets Wrap
summary: Asian stocks fell, tracking declines on Wall Street as investors remained wary of the AI trade ahead of Nvidia Corp.’s widely anticipated earnings and Anthropic PBC’s expected market debut.

title: Gold Steadies Near 14-Month Low as Inflation Pressure Persists
summary: Gold steadied after its lowest close since September 2025, under pressure from stubborn US inflation and losses on Wall Street.

title: Shamrock’s Lasalle: Different Ways To Invest in Sports
summary: Mike LaSalle, co-president and partner at Shamrock Capital, says the firm is assessing how upcoming sports contracts and shifting cash flows could create investment opportunities. Jason Sklar, partner at Shamrock Capital, talks about the financial shortages emerging in the sports industry and the role Shamrock Capital plays. They speak with Romaine Bostick on "The Close". (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Alzheimer's Will Be a "Treatable Condition," Says David Cameron
summary: David Cameron says that we have reached a "tipping point" where the combination of new Alzheimer's treatments and new biotech and pharmaceutical companies could result in someone alive today having their Alzheimer's condition 'reversed.' He speaks at a Bloomberg.com subscriber event in London. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: AirAsia, Malaysia Airports in $122 Million Debt Repayment Talks
summary: Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd. is in talks with AirAsia Group Bhd. about a repayment plan for 500 million ringgit ($122 million) owed by the low-cost airline, according to the airport operator.

title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Nov. 17
summary: Oil fell on signs supplies are outpacing demand, and as Vice President JD Vance signaled the US wants to avoid a prolonged war in Iran.

title: Colombia’s De La Espriella Vows Spending Cuts in Investor Pitch
summary: Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella pledged spending cuts and fiscal discipline as he sought to reassure investors amid one of the country’s most severe fiscal crises in decades.

title: Betterment CEO Sarah Levy on Plus Debut, New IRA Options
summary: Betterment CEO Sarah Levy discusses the company's newly announced Betterment Plus program, which brings together human guidance, individual stock trading, lending and partner products, and IRA custody. She speaks with Romaine Bostick and Vonnie Quinn on "The Close". (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Learfield’s Cole Gahagan on Economics of College Sports
summary: Cole Gahagan, president and CEO of Learfield, discusses how the company helps colleges generate commercial revenue and connect student-athletes with name, image and likeness (NIL) opportunities. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close". (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Bilt CEO on the Launch of “Neighborhood OS”
summary: Ankur Jain, CEO of Bilt, describes the company’s expansion from building services for residents to helping neighborhood businesses attract customers. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close". (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Billionaire Cheng Family Bankrolls Risky New World Rescue Plan
summary: The challenge of refinancing a mountain of debt at New World Development Co. last year was so daunting that bankers and company insiders dubbed the effort “Project Moon.”

title: Citigroup Targets $5 Trillion in Wealth From Rival Banks
summary: Citigroup Inc. is pursuing $5 trillion in wealth balances held by existing clients with rival firms, while ruling out major acquisitions, according to its wealth chief.

title: Brandon Copeland: Tale of Two Cities in College Sports
summary: Tennessee basketball players and their athletic department drafted a proposed term sheet that includes a salary cap, a spending floor and guaranteed pay—the first such collective bargaining framework in college sports. Brandon Copeland, former NFL linebacker and cofounder of athletes.org, who advised the negotiations, talks about what the players agreed to and whether the cap or the floor mattered more to them. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close". (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Measles' Comeback Could Be Just the Start
summary: The US has lost its long-standing measles eradication status. And this may be just the first public health victory to unravel under Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s watch, Bloomberg Opinion columnist Lisa Jarvis says. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Ex-Robinhood Software Engineer Pleads Guilty to Illegal Trading
summary: A former Robinhood Markets Inc. software engineer admitted to fraud for using nonpublic information to trade crypto-linked perpetual futures on a decentralized derivatives exchange.

title: Ending Alzheimer's with David Cameron
summary: Former Prime Minister of the United Kingdom David Cameron sits down with Bloomberg's David Merritt to talk about his podcast “Ending Alzheimer’s”, his personal journey and the increasingly bright future of Alzheimer’s treatment. He speaks with David Merritt, head of media editorial at Bloomberg, at a Bloomberg.com subscriber event in London. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Wells Fargo Sees S&P 500 at 8,200 By End of 2027 as Profits Slow
summary: Wells Fargo & Co.’s Ohsung Kwon set a year-end 2027 target of 8,200 for the S&P 500 Index, the lowest among Wall Street strategists who have published forecasts so far.

title: Billionaire Rinehart Boosts US Defense and SpaceX Holdings
summary: Gina Rinehart, Australia’s richest person, boosted American defense and aerospace stock holdings in the third quarter, along with her stake in Elon Musk’s SpaceX, as the market value of her US equity holdings increased to $5.7 billion.

title: China's Long-Term Auto Bet is Winning
summary: China has emerged as the global leader in electric vehicles, combining advanced technology, highly automated factories and a dense battery supply chain to produce increasingly sophisticated cars at competitive prices. Bloomberg Businessweek Editor Brad Stone says Chinese automakers have benefited from years of government support and long-term industrial planning, while shifting US policies have made it harder for American companies to make similar investments. (Source: Bloomberg)
